title: How One Computer Glitch Can Stall a Whole Airline
fb_caption: On Tuesday, US skies had their busiest day in 16 years, about 52,000 flights, officials said. Two days earlier, one computer system failed at one of the country's biggest airlines, and roughly 2,000 of its flights were delayed that day. Nothing was wrong with the planes. What was missing was the weight and balance math every airliner needs before takeoff. From there the dominoes can fall: slow hand calculations, full gates, arriving planes stuck on the taxiway, flights held at other airports, and crews running out of legal working hours. The system was back by Sunday afternoon, and the airline has not said what caused it. What's the longest you've ever been stuck at an airport? Tell us below.

beats.text: On Tuesday, America's skies had their busiest day in sixteen years: about fifty-two thousand flights, officials said. Two days earlier, one computer system failed at one of the country's biggest airlines, and roughly two thousand of its flights were delayed that day.
Nothing was wrong with the planes. The airline said most of the trouble traced to that one system, and what it does is math. So how can one glitch stall an airline? Watch the dominoes.

items: THE AIRLINE: MOST OF THE TROUBLE

overlays.text:
HOW ONE GLITCH CAN
STALL AN AIRLINE

beats.text: Domino one: no numbers. Before any airliner takes off, the crew needs its exact weight and its balance point. Those numbers set the takeoff speed and the engine power. No numbers, no takeoff.
Domino two: the slow way. The math can be done by hand. But that can mean counting bags one by one, at every single gate.
Domino three: the gates. A plane that can't leave is still parked. So the next arriving plane has nowhere to go, and it waits on the taxiway.
Domino four: the hub. To stop the pile-up, flights heading there can be held at their departure airports. That is called a ground stop.
Domino five: the clock. Pilots and flight attendants can only work a limited number of hours. When planes run late, crews can time out, and delays roll on long after the computer is fixed.
In this case, the system was back by Sunday afternoon. The airline has not said what caused it.
Takeaway: check the app before you leave home, rebook in the app instead of the line, and keep essentials in your carry-on.
